title: The Verdier dual of Weil complexes is a triangulated functor
statement: Let $k_0$ be a finite field, $k$ an algebraic closure, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ a prime and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, with structure map $a_X:X\to s_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$. Use the locally finite continuous coefficient-ring sheaf $B_X$, the abelian category $\mathcal W_X$ of pro-etale Weil module sheaves, and the bounded constructible full derived subcategory $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(X)\subset D(\mathcal W_X)$ of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], with its inherited triangulation. In particular, morphisms are derived morphisms of Weil sheaves, not morphisms between fixed pairs in a nonequivariant derived category. Use the actual compact-support functor $Ra_{X,0!}$, formed by equivariant extension by zero followed by derived proper pushforward along the chosen compactification, and the native derived internal Hom $R\mathcal Hom_X$ of [def-sf-derived-weil-category-and-operations]. Assume that $Ra_{X,0!}:\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(X)\to\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(s_0)$ has a right adjoint $Ra_X^!$ on these same categories. Put $\omega_X=Ra_X^!\mathbf1_0$, where $\mathbf1_0$ is the rank-one coefficient Weil sheaf in degree zero, as in that definition. Let $D_X$ be the restriction of $R\mathcal Hom_X(-,\omega_X)$ to $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(X)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(X)$, whose existence is supplied by [lem-sf-weil-verdier-dual-preserves-weil-complexes]. These are exactly the live `WeilComplex.dualizingComplex` and `WeilComplex.verdierDual`, with the chosen K-injective representatives specified by the definition. Then $D_X$ admits coherent commutation with all integer shifts making it triangulated: it carries distinguished triangles in $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(X)^{\mathrm{op}}$, with its opposite triangulated structure, to distinguished triangles in $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(X)$.

proof.text: Use $\mathcal W_X$, $B_X$ and the conjugation internal-Hom bifunctor $H$ of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework] and [def-sf-derived-weil-category-and-operations]. By [lem-sf-native-weil-constructible-abelian], $\mathcal W_X$ is Grothendieck abelian. Hence it has countable products by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-filtered-finite-limits], and every unbounded complex has a K-injective resolution by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective]. The bifunctor $H$ is additive in both variables: locally $(f+g)u=fu+gu$ and $u(f+g)=uf+ug$ for module maps, and these equalities commute with conjugation by the two Weil isomorphisms. They therefore hold for Weil internal-Hom maps. Choose the same representative $J=J_{\omega_X}$ and source replacement $R_X=\iota q^{-1}$ as in the definition, not a new resolution functor.

proof.text: The constructible heart in $\mathcal W_X$ contains zero and is invariant under isomorphisms, kernels, cokernels and extensions by [lem-sf-native-weil-constructible-abelian]. Thus [lem-sbc-cohomology-in-weak-serre-subcategory] applies to this heart: its bounded-cohomology derived subcategory is full triangulated with the inherited shifts and distinguished triangles. That subcategory is exactly $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(X)$ of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. The inclusion $j:\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(X)\to D(\mathcal W_X)$, and its opposite, use those inherited structures. This checks the full-triangulated-subcategory hypotheses needed at the final restriction.

proof.text: For an abstract abelian category with countable products and K-injective resolutions, take E to be the equivalence attached to the existing KInjectives.Qh. Apply [lem-sf-kinjective-replacement-triangulated] to E.inverse with E.unitIso and E.counitIso. The result supplies coherent shifts and exactness of this chosen replacement followed by inclusion, and of its opposite. In particular, it applies to precisely the quasi-inverse used by the unchanged DerivedCategory.bifunctorRHom definition.

proof.text: Fix I = DerivedCategory.kInjectiveRep(omega_X.obj). The theorem [lem-sf-bifunctor-homotopy-exact] supplies coherent shifts and triangulatedness of the leftOp of bifunctorHomHomotopyFunctor H I. Compose it with the opposite replacement from step 3, using [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-composite]. The composite is definitionally the signed bifunctorRHom H omega_X.obj actually used by ProEtaleWeilSheaf.derivedHom. No conversion to a second, standard-differential Hom complex is needed.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-restriction], namely ObjectProperty.isTriangulated_lift, to obtain coherent shifts and exactness of this full-subcategory lift.
